wa_mount_adams_wilson_glacier_headwall.approach: The Wilson Glacier sits on the east side of Mount Adams, descending from around 10,600 ft to a terminus near 7,400 ft — a less-visited, less-documented flank than the standard south or north-side routes. Parties reach it via the Cold Springs/South Climb trailhead (5,600 ft, FS Rd 8040 off FS Rd 80): follow the South Climb Trail #183 about 1 mile up an old road bed to the junction with the Round the Mountain Trail, then instead of continuing north toward Lunch Counter, follow Round the Mountain Trail east below Crescent Glacier onto Yakama Nation land, where a separate tribal permit is required and the trail ends at Hellroaring Canyon; the way on, north around the mountain's eastern flank toward the Klickitat and Wilson glacier basins, is a long off-trail traverse with route-finding, creek crossings, and exposure to rockfall directly below the headwall's cliff bands. Expect a full day just to reach camp in Avalanche Valley, below the Rusk and Wilson glaciers, before a summit attempt.

approach_variants.name: Cold Springs and the Round the Mountain Trail east around the mountain
approach_variants.notes:
From the Cold Springs and South Climb trailhead at about 5,600 ft at the end of the forest road north of Trout Lake, follow South Climb Trail #183 about a mile up an old road bed to the junction with the Round the Mountain Trail.

Instead of continuing north toward the Lunch Counter, follow the Round the Mountain Trail east and then north, contouring below the Crescent Glacier and around the mountain's eastern flank toward the Klickitat and Wilson glacier basins, crossing the Klickitat Glacier and Big Muddy Creek on the way. This is a long, mostly off-trail traverse with route-finding, creek crossings, and exposure to rockfall directly below the headwall's cliff bands.

The Wilson descends from around 10,600 ft to a terminus near 7,400 ft, and it is split by a rock rib. Expect a full day to reach camp in Avalanche Valley, below the Rusk and Wilson glaciers, before any summit attempt.

This is one of the least-visited and least-documented flanks of the mountain. The descent is not a reversal: parties top out and come down the standard South Climb to Cold Springs.
approach_variants.season: Roughly May-Jun for the headwall itself; the surrounding east-side walls are rockfall-prone once warm
hazards: Persistent rockfall from the east-side cliff bands, directly over the contouring approach
A steep ice and snow headwall with serac hazard
A long, mostly off-trail traverse with creek crossings and route-finding, and a full day just to reach camp
Rarely climbed, so conditions cannot be inferred from recent traffic and rescue would be slow
approach_variants.baseFinding:
The decision happens about a mile from the car and it is a turning, not an arrival. At the junction of the South Climb Trail with the Round the Mountain Trail, the standard South Spur route goes north toward the Lunch Counter; this route goes east. If you are climbing toward the Lunch Counter, you are on the standard South Climb and this route is already behind you.

That is the one error worth guarding, because it is recoverable only by walking back down. Everything after it is a long contour.

The positive test at the base is a glacier split by a rock rib. The Wilson runs from about 10,600 ft down to about 7,400 ft and a rock rib divides it. A headwall above a glacier that is bisected by a rib is the confirmation. An unbroken glacier with no rib in it is not the Wilson.

The second positive is aspect and it is the coarsest but most reliable: you must be on the east side of the mountain. Going around the eastern flank is the whole approach. If the sun is rising behind the mountain rather than in front of you, you have not come far enough round.

The negative that matters for safety rather than navigation: the contour runs directly beneath cliff bands that shed rock. It is a place to keep moving. Persistent rockfall on these east-side headwalls is among the reasons most of them remain unrepeated, so a rope-length of comfortable ground is not evidence the ground above you is quiet.

What being on a neighbouring basin looks like: coming round from the south you meet the Klickitat first, the biggest glacier on this side, then the Rusk; the Wilson lies north of the Rusk, above Avalanche Valley. A big glacier met soon after leaving the Bird Creek side is the Klickitat, not the Wilson.

days.note: An early alpine start from Avalanche Valley, up the Wilson Glacier to the headwall below Roosevelt Cliff (starts around 10,800 ft) — a steep, avalanche/icefall-fed line considered one of Adams' most serious routes. Top out and descend the South Climb to Cold Springs.

itinerary.totalNote: A 2-day trip: a long approach round the east side to Avalanche Valley, then a serious, early alpine-start headwall climb (~13 hr) and a descent of the South Climb to the car.
